_note: Curated, hand-verified POIs across NV/CA/AZ/UT. Coordinates are real (lat,lon). 'kind' is the headline type; 'services' is what you can do there (gas/lodging/food). Encounters carry language+voice for Kokoro NPCs. Arbitrary street addresses are resolved live via OSM geocoding; this set seeds the authored map and the survival lattice.

start.name: SEMA — LVCC North Hall
start.blurb: The show floor at twenty minutes to close. Compressors, a rev-limiter slapping the rafters, ten thousand people who all think they know cars. She's on the turntable, white under the lights — and the placard doesn't mention she talks.

pois.name: Paradise Road Chevron, behind the LVCC North Hall
pois.blurb: Neon on wet asphalt. The show is still roaring two blocks back. The pump island is empty and the needle is near E.

pois.name: Las Vegas
pois.blurb: The Strip, the convention halls, ten thousand cameras. A bright place to be a car nobody can quite account for.

pois.name: Las Vegas Motor Speedway
pois.blurb: A 1.5-mile tri-oval and a dragstrip out in the desert north of town.

pois.name: Spring Mountain Motorsports Ranch, Pahrump
pois.blurb: Members' road course out past the Spring Mountains. Close enough to taste, far enough to strand you on a bad tank.

pois.name: Pahrump
pois.blurb: Casinos, a winery, and the last cheap gas before the Death Valley road.

pois.name: Valley of Fire State Park
pois.blurb: Aztec sandstone the color of a struck match. No fuel out here. Plan it.

pois.name: Mesquite
pois.blurb: Last Nevada town on I-15 before the Arizona slot and the Utah line. Fill here for Zion.

pois.name: Glendale / Moapa
pois.blurb: An off-ramp, a truck stop, a reservation smoke shop. Fuel on the I-15 run.

pois.name: Beatty
pois.blurb: Gateway to Death Valley from the north. Wild burros on the road at dusk.

pois.name: Primm
pois.blurb: A border casino with a roller coaster, straddling the California line on I-15.

pois.name: Laughlin
pois.blurb: Riverboat casinos on the Colorado, cheaper than Vegas, hot as a griddle.

pois.name: Hoover Dam / Boulder City
pois.blurb: 726 feet of Depression-era concrete holding back Lake Mead. Last gas in Boulder City.

pois.name: Tonopah
pois.blurb: Old silver town, the darkest skies in the lower 48, halfway up the middle of nowhere.

pois.name: Rachel / Extraterrestrial Highway
pois.blurb: The Little A'Le'Inn and 98 miles of empty SR-375. Top off before you commit; there is nothing out here.

pois.name: Ely
pois.blurb: A railroad town on the Loneliest Road, last stop before Great Basin.

pois.name: Great Basin National Park
pois.blurb: Wheeler Peak, bristlecone pines older than writing, the Lehman Caves. Almost nobody comes.

pois.name: Reno
pois.blurb: The Biggest Little City, up against the Sierra. A long way from the show.

pois.name: Carson City
pois.blurb: The quiet capital under the eastern slope of the Sierra.

pois.name: the registered address — a quiet street in Carson City
pois.blurb: A '70s ranch house up under the foothills, blinds drawn, a month of newspapers on the step. The name on the registration is the name on the mailbox. Nobody home — they're in Portugal till the end of the month. There's a brown Datsun under a sheet in the garage.

pois.name: Baker
pois.blurb: The world's tallest thermometer and a Greek diner. Gateway to Death Valley from I-15.

pois.name: Barstow
pois.blurb: Where the desert highways knot together. Route 66 murals, a rail yard, cheap motels.

pois.name: Calico Ghost Town
pois.blurb: A silver boomtown that died and got bought by Knott's. Plank sidewalks above Barstow.

pois.name: Needles
pois.blurb: Where I-40 crosses the Colorado into California. Brutally hot, friendly enough.

pois.name: Death Valley NP (Furnace Creek)
pois.blurb: 282 feet below sea level, the hottest place on Earth. Gas here costs what they want it to.

pois.name: Stovepipe Wells
pois.blurb: A dune, a saloon, and a pump in the middle of Death Valley.

pois.name: Mojave
pois.blurb: Wind turbines, a spaceport, and rows of mothballed airliners in the dry air.

pois.name: Willow Springs International Raceway
pois.blurb: 'The Fastest Road in the West.' Nine turns of old California tarmac near Rosamond.

pois.name: Buttonwillow Raceway Park
pois.blurb: Flat, technical club track in the cotton fields west of Bakersfield.

pois.name: Auto Club Speedway (Fontana)
pois.blurb: A two-mile D-oval in the Inland Empire smog, on borrowed time.

pois.name: Chuckwalla Valley Raceway
pois.blurb: Desert road course out by Desert Center. Bring your own everything.

pois.name: WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca
pois.blurb: The Corkscrew. Eleven turns dropping through the Monterey hills like a dare.

pois.name: Thunderhill Raceway Park
pois.blurb: Five miles of track in the rice country near Willows, home of the 25-hour race.

pois.name: Sonoma Raceway
pois.blurb: Wine-country hills folded into a road course at the top of the bay.

pois.name: Joshua Tree National Park
pois.blurb: Where the Mojave meets the Colorado desert and the trees throw their arms up. No gas inside.

pois.name: Yosemite National Park
pois.blurb: El Capitan, Half Dome, the granite cathedral. Tioga Pass closes with the snow.

pois.name: Sequoia National Park
pois.blurb: The biggest living things that have ever stood. The road up is all switchbacks.

pois.name: Kings Canyon National Park
pois.blurb: A glacial gorge deeper than the Grand Canyon, and far emptier.

pois.name: Disneyland (Anaheim)
pois.blurb: The original. A monorail, a Matterhorn, and a parking structure the size of a town.

pois.name: Knott's Berry Farm (Buena Park)
pois.blurb: The boysenberry kingdom. Wooden coasters and a ghost town that owns Calico.

pois.name: Six Flags Magic Mountain (Valencia)
pois.blurb: Nineteen coasters stacked on a hill above the 5. The thrill-ride capital of the world.

pois.name: Universal Studios Hollywood
pois.blurb: A working backlot you can ride through, perched above the 101.

pois.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
pois.blurb: The Giant Dipper, salt air, and 1907 still running on the sand.

pois.name: SeaWorld San Diego
pois.blurb: Mission Bay, coasters, and the smell of the cold Pacific.

pois.name: Santa Monica Pier
pois.blurb: The Pacific Wheel and the end of Route 66, where the road runs out of country.

pois.name: Los Angeles
pois.blurb: Twelve million people and a freeway for every one of them.

pois.name: Little Tokyo, Los Angeles
pois.blurb: Lanterns over First Street, a mochi shop, a woman who does not switch to English when you stumble.
pois.npc: the okamisan at a Little Tokyo counter

pois.name: East Los Angeles
pois.blurb: Mariachi Plaza, taquerias, a mechanic who talks to your engine before he talks to you.

pois.name: Artesia / Little India
pois.blurb: Pioneer Boulevard: sari shops, sweets, and a chai cart that runs on its own time.
pois.npc: the chai-cart auntie on Pioneer Blvd

pois.name: San Diego
pois.blurb: Navy gray and surf gold, the last big city before the line.

pois.name: San Francisco
pois.blurb: Forty-three hills and the fog coming in over them. Park facing the curb or lose your tires.

pois.name: Japantown, San Francisco
pois.blurb: The Peace Pagoda, a bookstore, a ramen line. If you drove all this way, this is who you came to hear.
pois.npc: a shopkeeper in the Japan Center

pois.name: Chinatown, San Francisco
pois.blurb: The oldest Chinatown in the country. Grant Avenue, a tea seller who measures you with her eyes.
pois.npc: a tea seller on Grant Avenue

pois.name: North Beach, San Francisco
pois.blurb: Espresso, City Lights bookstore, an old man who calls every car bella.
pois.npc: a cafe owner on Columbus Avenue

pois.name: The Mission, San Francisco
pois.blurb: Murals down every alley and the best taqueria argument in the state.

pois.name: Bakersfield
pois.blurb: Oil derricks, the Bakersfield Sound, and the bottom of the Central Valley.

pois.name: Fresno
pois.blurb: The gateway to three national parks, flat and patient in the haze.

pois.name: Bishop
pois.blurb: The Eastern Sierra hub. Erick Schat's bakery, the High Sierra throwing shadows by four.

pois.name: Lone Pine
pois.blurb: Under Mt. Whitney, where a thousand Westerns were shot in the Alabama Hills.

pois.name: Lee Vining / Tioga Pass
pois.blurb: Mono Lake's tufa towers and the eastern gate to Yosemite, 9,943 feet up when it's open.

pois.name: Palm Springs
pois.blurb: Mid-century glass under the San Jacintos, a tram to the snow line above the heat.

pois.name: Grand Canyon NP (South Rim)
pois.blurb: A mile straight down and ten miles across. Gas and rooms at the village, if you booked.

pois.name: Grand Canyon NP (North Rim)
pois.blurb: A thousand feet higher, far emptier, closed once the snow comes.

pois.name: Flagstaff
pois.blurb: Ponderosa pines at 7,000 feet, Route 66 and the railroad, snow on the peaks.

pois.name: Williams
pois.blurb: The last town on Route 66 to be bypassed, and the rail gateway to the Grand Canyon.

pois.name: Kingman
pois.blurb: Heart of Route 66 Arizona, a crossroads of I-40 and the road up from Vegas.

pois.name: Lake Havasu City
pois.blurb: Someone bought the actual London Bridge and shipped it here, stone by stone.

pois.name: Sedona
pois.blurb: Red-rock spires, art galleries, and people who will tell you about the vortexes.

pois.name: Page / Horseshoe Bend
pois.blurb: Antelope Canyon's light shafts, the green river bending 270 degrees under your boots.

pois.name: Phoenix
pois.blurb: The Valley of the Sun, a grid of warm light spreading to every horizon.

pois.name: Castles N' Coasters (Phoenix)
pois.blurb: Arizona's last big amusement park: four mini-golf courses and the Desert Storm coaster.

pois.name: Tucson
pois.blurb: Saguaro forests, the old Spanish presidio, the Sonoran desert in bloom after rain.

pois.name: Nogales
pois.blurb: The border. The fence runs right through town and the language doesn't stop at it.
pois.npc: a vendor at the line in Nogales

pois.name: Saguaro National Park
pois.blurb: A forest of giant cactus standing watch over Tucson, arms raised against the dusk.

pois.name: Petrified Forest National Park
pois.blurb: Stone logs of a vanished jungle and the banded Painted Desert. No services, long miles.

pois.name: Monument Valley
pois.blurb: The mittens and the buttes on the Navajo line, the most filmed horizon in America.

pois.name: Meteor Crater
pois.blurb: A 50,000-year-old hole in the desert, three-quarters of a mile across, off old 66.

pois.name: St. George
pois.blurb: The first Utah town off I-15, red rock and a tabernacle. Fill here for Zion or Bryce.

pois.name: Springdale (Zion gate)
pois.blurb: The little town at the mouth of Zion Canyon. Shuttle, lodges, the cliffs leaning in overhead.

pois.name: Zion National Park
pois.blurb: Navajo sandstone walls 2,000 feet high, the Narrows, Angels Landing. The trip everyone tries to make on a splash of gas.

pois.name: Cedar City
pois.blurb: Festival town below the high plateaus, the turnoff for Bryce and Cedar Breaks.

pois.name: Kanab
pois.blurb: 'Little Hollywood,' the hub between Zion, Bryce, the Grand Canyon's North Rim, and the Wave.

pois.name: Bryce Canyon National Park
pois.blurb: An amphitheater of orange hoodoos at 8,000 feet. Cold at night, even in summer.

pois.name: Capitol Reef National Park
pois.blurb: A hundred-mile wrinkle in the earth, orchards in the desert, petroglyphs on the cliffs.

pois.name: Goblin Valley State Park
pois.blurb: A valley of mushroom-shaped hoodoos you can walk among, like a planet left unfinished.

pois.name: Moab
pois.blurb: Slickrock and the Colorado, mountain bikes and 4x4s, the base for two national parks.

pois.name: Arches National Park
pois.blurb: Over 2,000 stone arches, Delicate Arch alone on the rim against the La Sals.

pois.name: Canyonlands National Park
pois.blurb: Where the Green and the Colorado carve the earth into Islands in the Sky. No gas, no water.

pois.name: Salt Lake City
pois.blurb: The grid laid out from a temple, the Wasatch hard against the eastern edge.

pois.name: Lagoon Amusement Park (Farmington)
pois.blurb: Utah's own park since 1886: a wooden coaster from 1921 still rattling north of Salt Lake.

pois.name: Park City
pois.blurb: Old silver mines turned ski resort, Main Street steep with money and snow.

pois.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
pois.blurb: Thirty thousand acres of dead-flat salt where land-speed records are made. The horizon curves.

pois.name: Fallon / NAS Fallon
pois.blurb: Naval Air Station Fallon — TOPGUN moved here. Hornets tear the desert sky open low and loud.

pois.name: The Sphere, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: A 366-foot eyeball made of LEDs, blinking at the freeway. It is looking at you. It is always looking.

pois.name: Fremont Street, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: Old downtown under a canopy of a billion bulbs, a zipline screaming overhead, a cowboy made of neon.

pois.name: Seven Magic Mountains
pois.blurb: Stacks of fluorescent boulders rising out of the Jean dry lake, somebody's idea south of Vegas.

pois.name: Golden Gate Bridge
pois.blurb: International orange swallowed by fog. The towers come and go like a rumor.

pois.name: Racetrack Playa (Death Valley)
pois.blurb: The sailing stones. Rocks that move themselves across the mud and leave trails, and no one watching.

pois.name: Salvation Mountain
pois.blurb: A hand-painted adobe hill of love and scripture out by the Salton Sea, next to a town with no laws.

pois.name: Amargosa Opera House (Death Valley Junction)
pois.blurb: A lone opera house in the empty desert where a dancer painted herself an audience on the walls.

pois.name: Goldfield ghost town
pois.blurb: Once the biggest city in Nevada, now a few hundred souls, a haunted hotel, and a yard of welded art cars.

pois.name: The Integratron
pois.blurb: A white dome built from alien instructions for rejuvenation and time travel. Sound baths now. Sure.

pois.name: Madonna Inn, San Luis Obispo
pois.blurb: 110 rooms, no two alike, pink as a wound, a urinal that's a waterfall. You have to stay somewhere.

pois.name: Bigfoot country (Willow Creek)
pois.blurb: Self-proclaimed Bigfoot capital. A giant carved sasquatch by the road, and the trees lean in close.

pois.name: Area 51 back gate
pois.blurb: A cattle guard, a white truck on a hill, cameras on poles, and a sign that promises deadly force.

pois.name: koiNOya — Richmond
pois.blurb: A cluttered Edo-era relic shop in Richmond: naginata and ceremonial blades racked like umbrellas, each one carved with a card suit. Where Ace was born.

pois.name: AiSha Garage — Downtown Oakland
pois.blurb: A 1926 red-brick garage downtown, AiSHALLC hand-painted across the roofline, a kanji on the roll-up door, the skyline rising behind. Where Ace grew up.

pois.name: Petersen Automotive Museum, LA
pois.blurb: A red ribbon of steel wrapped around four floors of cars. She asks to idle out front a while.

pois.name: The Neon Museum, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: The Boneyard: dead casino signs laid out under the desert sky, still glowing if you squint.

pois.name: The Getty Center, LA
pois.blurb: Travertine and a tram up the hill — art, gardens, and the whole basin laid out below.

pois.name: Heard Museum, Phoenix
pois.blurb: The finest collection of Native American art in the Southwest, in a quiet Spanish-revival courtyard.

pois.name: Natural History Museum of Utah, SLC
pois.blurb: A copper-skinned ark built into the Wasatch foothills, full of dinosaurs and deep time.

pois.name: Pinball Hall of Fame, Las Vegas
pois.blurb: A warehouse of playable machines back to the 1950s. Bring quarters; leave the heat outside.

pois.name: Monterey
pois.blurb: Cannery Row, the kelp tanks, 17-Mile Drive. The cypress lean into the fog like they're listening.

pois.name: Long Beach
pois.blurb: The Queen Mary at anchor, the port cranes like grazing dinosaurs, the salvage yards inland.

pois.name: Livermore
pois.blurb: Wine country gone to office parks and self-storage. A row of roll-up doors keeps more secrets than any vault.

pois.name: San Jose
pois.blurb: The capital of Silicon Valley, flat and warm and endless.

pois.name: Berkeley
pois.blurb: The university, the hills, the smell of eucalyptus and protest.

pois.name: Sacramento
pois.blurb: The state capital under the delta breeze, old gold-rush bones downtown.

pois.name: Stockton
pois.blurb: A deep-water port ninety miles from the sea, asphalt shimmering in the valley heat.

pois.name: Santa Barbara
pois.blurb: Red-tile roofs, the Riviera of the West, the 101 running right along the surf.

pois.name: Ventura
pois.blurb: A pier, a point break, and the Channel Islands floating offshore.

pois.name: Oceanside
pois.blurb: Marine town, longboards, the smell of diesel and sunscreen.

pois.name: Riverside
pois.blurb: The Mission Inn and the orange groves that built it, inland and bright.

pois.name: Pasadena
pois.blurb: Craftsman bungalows, the Rose Bowl, the Colorado Street bridge over the arroyo.

pois.name: Palm Desert
pois.blurb: Golf and glass under the Santa Rosas, El Paseo for the snowbirds.

pois.name: Gilroy
pois.blurb: Garlic capital of the world; you smell it before the off-ramp.

pois.name: Napa
pois.blurb: Vines in tidy rows, tasting rooms, the wine train rattling north.

pois.name: Half Moon Bay
pois.blurb: Pumpkins, Mavericks' big surf, Highway 1 hugging the cliff edge.

pois.name: Redding
pois.blurb: Top of the valley under Mount Shasta, the Sundial Bridge over the Sacramento.

pois.name: Berlin–Ichthyosaur State Park
pois.blurb: A silver-rush ghost town nobody bothered to tear down — and behind it, under a shed, the bones of fifty-foot sea monsters that died here when Nevada was an ocean.

pois.name: Winnemucca
pois.blurb: Winnemucca is the only incorporated city in Humboldt County, Nevada, United States, of which it is also the county seat, encompassing approximately half of the total population of…
pois.beat: Winnemucca. Half of Humboldt County lives inside this one set of city limits — the only incorporated city the county has — and the other half is out there in the dark somewhere. I respect both decisions.

pois.name: Elko
pois.blurb: Elko is a city in and the county seat of Elko County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Elko. Twenty-one miles from town, Lamoille Canyon runs up into the Ruby Mountains, and people come here for the climb. I'm built low for a reason; the valley suits me fine.

pois.name: Wells
pois.blurb: Wells is a small city in Elko County, in northeast Nevada in the western United States.
pois.beat: Wells. This is where U.S. 93 meets Interstate 80, and the whole town is arranged around that decision. Junction towns don't keep you — that's their kindness, not their failure.

pois.name: West Wendover
pois.blurb: West Wendover is a city in Elko County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: West Wendover. East of the last block, the Great Salt Lake Desert takes over — white, flat, patient as arithmetic. Salt eats cars politely, over years; we admire it from the curb.

pois.name: Battle Mountain
pois.blurb: Battle Mountain is an unincorporated town in and the county seat of Lander County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Battle Mountain. Gold mining pays for everything here — shine pulled out of dark ground so that somewhere far away can glitter. I have some sympathy for the ore.

pois.name: Lovelock
pois.blurb: Lovelock is the county seat of Pershing County, Nevada, United States, in which it is the only incorporated city.
pois.beat: Lovelock. The only incorporated city in all of Pershing County, county seat the way the last one standing makes captain. A name like that ought to draw more company.

pois.name: Eureka
pois.blurb: Eureka is an unincorporated town and census-designated place in and the county seat of Eureka County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Eureka. An Opera House, out here — somebody looked at all this distance and decided the silence deserved an answer with velvet seats. I'll idle outside and listen for an overture.

pois.name: Austin
pois.blurb: Austin is an unincorporated census-designated place in and the former county seat of Lander County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Austin. We're 6,575 feet up the western slope of the Toiyabe Range, and my carburetors have noticed the air comes rationed at this height. Towns this high don't grow; they hold.

pois.name: Hawthorne
pois.blurb: Hawthorne is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Mineral County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Hawthorne. Everything this town earns, it earns from the Army Depot next door — a living made of keeping munitions company. People drive gently here, and tonight so do I.

pois.name: Mina
pois.blurb: Mina is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Mineral County in west-central Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Mina. A hundred and twenty-seven people at the last census, which means tonight's population is whoever left a light on. Nobody out here watches you arrive — that's the gift.

pois.name: Virginia City
pois.blurb: Virginia City is a historic town in Storey County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Virginia City. In 1859 the Comstock Lode came up out of this mountain and the whole country leaned in to look. The silver's long gone; the leaning you can still feel.

pois.name: Genoa
pois.blurb: Genoa is an unincorporated town in Douglas County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Genoa. Nevada's oldest bar is in this town, which makes it the place where the state first admitted it needed a drink. I run on something stronger, but I understand the impulse.

pois.name: Gardnerville
pois.blurb: Gardnerville is an unincorporated town in Douglas County, Nevada, United States, adjacent to the county seat of Minden.
pois.beat: Gardnerville. It leans right up against Minden, the county seat — two towns so close the border is mostly an opinion. Twice the quiet on one road; we could sleep here.

pois.name: Yerington
pois.blurb: Yerington is a city in Lyon County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Yerington. A whole town named for the superintendent of the Virginia and Truckee Railroad, which tells you what counted as power out here — the man who ran the trains. I roll in a century off the timetable; the name on the sign is still his.

pois.name: Fernley
pois.blurb: Fernley is a city in Lyon County, Nevada, United States, and part of the Reno–Tahoe–Sparks metropolitan area CSA.
pois.beat: Fernley. A city only since 2001 — as municipalities go, it's younger than the oil stains on my floor pans. The streets still wear that unconvinced look new towns have.

pois.name: Boulder City
pois.blurb: Boulder City is a city in Clark County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Boulder City. One of exactly two places in Nevada where gambling is banned — a whole state built on odds, and this town simply declined to play. I admire anything that knows what it refuses.

pois.name: Searchlight
pois.blurb: Searchlight is an unincorporated town and census-designated place (CDP) in Clark County, Nevada, United States, at the topographic saddle between two mountain ranges.
pois.beat: Searchlight. We crest into the saddle between two mountain ranges and the town is just sitting there in the notch, like something the wind set down and forgot. I cut the radio out of respect.

pois.name: Alamo
pois.blurb: Alamo is an unincorporated town in Lincoln County, Nevada, United States, about 90 miles (140 km) north of Las Vegas along U.S.
pois.beat: Alamo. Ninety miles north of Las Vegas and you can feel every one of them in the quiet — Route 93 just lays itself down flat here and waits. Top off the tank; the road north doesn't apologize.

pois.name: Caliente
pois.blurb: Caliente, formerly known as Culverwell and Calientes, is a city in Lincoln County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Caliente. Named for the hot springs — Spanish for exactly what it says, a town that puts the truth right on the sign. Steam under the ground, cold stars over it. My coolant appreciates the symmetry.

pois.name: Pioche
pois.blurb: Pioche is an unincorporated town in Lincoln County, Nevada, United States, approximately 180 miles (290 km) northeast of Las Vegas.
pois.beat: Pioche. The highway bypasses the town center just to the east, so the whole country is passing Pioche by, all day, every day, at seventy. I take the old road in. Somebody should.

pois.name: Overton
pois.blurb: Overton is a community that is part of the unincorporated town of Moapa Valley in Clark County, Nevada.
pois.beat: Overton. A town with two airports — Perkins Field and Echo Bay — which tells you how badly people out here want to leave the ground. I keep all four tires on it, on principle.

pois.name: Gerlach
pois.blurb: Gerlach, Nevada is a census-designated place (CDP) in Washoe County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Gerlach. The paperwork files this place under the Reno–Sparks metropolitan area, which is the driest joke a federal form has ever told. The dark out here is total; my headlights feel like a confession.

pois.name: Jackpot
pois.blurb: Jackpot is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in Elko County, Nevada, United States.
pois.beat: Jackpot. Built less than a mile from the Idaho line, so the neighbors can lose a paycheck and still be home by midnight. Every light in town is somebody's optimism, wired and humming. None of it is for me.

pois.name: Amargosa Valley
pois.blurb: Amargosa Valley is an unincorporated town located on U.S.
pois.beat: Amargosa Valley. Unincorporated — the town never bothered drawing a line around itself, just Route 95, some mailboxes, and all of Nye County's sky. I sympathize. Nobody ever drew a line around me either.

pois.name: Truckee
pois.blurb: Truckee is an incorporated town in Nevada County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Truckee. California town, Nevada County — the border getting one last joke in before the pass. Cold air, tall pines, and every roof rack in this parking lot cost more than I did new.

pois.name: South Lake Tahoe
pois.blurb: South Lake Tahoe is the most populous city in El Dorado County, California, United States, in the Sierra Nevada mountains.
pois.beat: South Lake Tahoe. Five miles of city strung along Route 50 at the lake's southern edge — a town shaped exactly like the road that made it. I know the feeling. We roll the whole length just to be sure.

pois.name: Mammoth Lakes
pois.blurb: Mammoth Lakes is the only incorporated town in Mono County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Mammoth Lakes. Seven thousand eight hundred and eighty feet, and my engine notices before I do — old carburetors remember sea level the way some people remember being young. I lean myself out and climb anyway.

pois.name: Bridgeport
pois.blurb: Bridgeport is an unincorporated community and a census-designated place (CDP) in and the county seat of Mono County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Bridgeport. All of Mono County's law and paperwork lives here — the county seat, kept in a town short enough to miss while adjusting a mirror. I slow down anyway. It seems like the kind of place that notices.

pois.name: Bodie
pois.blurb: Bodie is a ghost town in the Bodie Hills east of the Sierra Nevada mountain range in Mono County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Bodie. It boomed in 1876 on one profitable vein and then stopped, mid-sentence, the way only mining towns and engines can. I cut the motor and let the silence come in like it owns the place. It does.

pois.name: Independence
pois.blurb: Independence is an unincorporated census-designated place in and the county seat of Inyo County, California.
pois.beat: Independence. The census counted 593 here last time, down from 669 the decade before — a town letting go of itself a few hands at a time. Out here the name stops sounding like a boast and starts sounding like a condition.

pois.name: Ridgecrest
pois.blurb: Ridgecrest is a city in Kern County, California, United States, along U.S.
pois.beat: Ridgecrest. Next door, the Navy keeps China Lake, its weapons station, so everything overhead is fast, federal, and not interested in me. For once I'm the slow one in the valley. It's restful.

pois.name: Trona
pois.blurb: Trona is an unincorporated community in San Bernardino County, California.
pois.beat: Trona. The town is named for the mineral they scrape out of the dry lakebed next door — a place that introduces itself by what it can be mined for. The air has a chemical sweetness I'll taste for miles.

pois.name: Tehachapi
pois.blurb: Tehachapi is a city in Kern County, California, United States, in the Tehachapi Mountains, at an elevation of 3,970 feet (1,210 m), between the San Joaquin Valley and the Mojave D…
pois.beat: Tehachapi. The sign says elevation 3,970, and the temperature needle says we earned every foot of it. Mountain air is kind to an old straight-six — first deep breath I've taken since the flats.

pois.name: Lancaster
pois.blurb: Lancaster is a charter city in northern Los Angeles County, in the Antelope Valley of the western Mojave Desert in Southern California, United States.
pois.beat: Lancaster. Twinned with Palmdale, the way my headlights are twinned — side by side, pointed the same direction, never quite meeting. Desert cities sprawl instead of rising. Easier to disappear into.

pois.name: Victorville
pois.blurb: Victorville is a city in the Victor Valley in San Bernardino County, California.
pois.beat: Victorville. 134,810 people at the last count, and not one of them looks up as we pass. High-desert towns perfect the art of not asking. I could learn something here.

pois.name: Twentynine Palms
pois.blurb: Twentynine Palms is a city in San Bernardino County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Twentynine Palms. A doorway town — one of the ways into Joshua Tree, so everything here points outward at the dark. I idle well in places built for passing through.

pois.name: Indio
pois.blurb: Indio is a city in Riverside County, California, United States, in the Coachella Valley of Southern California's Colorado Desert region.
pois.beat: Indio. Ninety-eight miles of open desert between here and Blythe, and the fuel gauge has already done the arithmetic. We fill up here. That kind of empty doesn't forgive romantics.

pois.name: El Centro
pois.blurb: El Centro is a city in and the county seat of Imperial County, California, United States.
pois.beat: El Centro. County seat of Imperial County, and the word imperial is doing heavy lifting out here in the flat heat. Seats of power always feel like waiting rooms to me. We won't wait long.

pois.name: Blythe
pois.blurb: Blythe is a city in eastern Riverside County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Blythe. Named for Thomas Henry Blythe, whoever he was — towns out here wear dead men's names like borrowed coats. I can feel the river before I see it, the air going soft against the windshield.

pois.name: Julian
pois.blurb: Julian is a census-designated place (CDP) in San Diego County, California, which developed as a classic gold rush boomtown in the 1870s after gold was discovered by Fred Coleman, …
pois.beat: Julian. Fred Coleman found gold here in the 1870s, and the town has been politely cashing that check ever since. Boomtowns that survive learn to sell the memory instead of the metal.

pois.name: Borrego Springs
pois.blurb: Borrego Springs is a census-designated place (CDP) in northeastern San Diego County, California.
pois.beat: Borrego Springs. Surrounded on every side by Anza-Borrego Desert State Park — a pocket of porch lights with wilderness for a moat. Towns like this don't lock much. The desert does it for them.

pois.name: Temecula
pois.blurb: Temecula is a city in southwestern Riverside County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Temecula. A city only since December 1989, which makes it younger than my paint. Everything here is new and pleased about it — the kind of place that remembers its own ribbon-cutting. We'll be older somewhere else by morning.

pois.name: Ojai
pois.blurb: Ojai is a city in Ventura County, California.
pois.beat: Ojai. Ten miles long and three wide, the whole valley — small enough that the mountains hear everything. I come in off-throttle, quiet as a 1972 anything can manage.

pois.name: Paso Robles
pois.blurb: Paso Robles, officially El Paso de Robles, is a city in San Luis Obispo County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Paso Robles. Officially El Paso de Robles — the pass of the oaks — but the town trimmed its own name down to something that fits in a hurry. I understand. I've answered to shorter names myself.

pois.name: San Luis Obispo
pois.blurb: San Luis Obispo is a city in and the county seat of San Luis Obispo County, California, United States.
pois.beat: San Luis Obispo. Roughly halfway between the Bay Area and Los Angeles, which makes this the exact spot where both stop mattering. Halfway is where resolve gets tested. Mine idles fine.

pois.name: San Simeon
pois.blurb: San Simeon is an unincorporated community on the Pacific coast of San Luis Obispo County, California, United States.
pois.beat: San Simeon. Population 445 — fewer people than some parking structures I've slept in. The Pacific takes up the rest of the room here, and tonight that arrangement suits me.

pois.name: Big Sur
pois.blurb: Big Sur is a rugged and mountainous section of the Central Coast of the U.S.
pois.beat: Big Sur. The Santa Lucias come straight out of the Pacific here, no negotiation, and the road has to apologize its way along the cliffs. This is what steering was invented for. I won't pretend to be calm.

pois.name: Salinas
pois.blurb: Salinas is a city in and the county seat of Monterey County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Salinas. Most populous city in Monterey County, which surprises people who only know the county by its coastline. Inland is where the work lives. I like a town with grease under its nails.

pois.name: Santa Maria
pois.blurb: Santa Maria is a city in Santa Barbara County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Santa Maria. They named a whole style of barbecue after this town, and the smoke on the evening air is still making the argument — strong enough to taste through a closed vent. I don't eat; I slowed down anyway.

pois.name: Solvang
pois.blurb: Solvang is a city in Santa Barbara County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Solvang. Danish Capital of America, the signs insist — an entire town doing an impression of somewhere else and never once breaking character. I'm a Japanese car wearing an English name; I withhold judgment.

pois.name: Santa Rosa
pois.blurb: Santa Rosa is a city in and the county seat of Sonoma County, United States, in the North Bay region of the Bay Area in California.
pois.beat: Santa Rosa. Biggest city in all the Wine Country, which means the romance got zoned, signaled, and metered a long while back. Nobody here looks twice at an old coupe, and that suits me fine.

pois.name: Petaluma
pois.blurb: Petaluma is a city in Sonoma County, California, United States, located in the North Bay region of the San Francisco Bay Area.
pois.beat: Petaluma. Fifty-nine thousand and change, says the census, and tonight the North Bay has every one of them indoors. Streets this empty make my engine sound like a confession.

pois.name: Mendocino
pois.blurb: Mendocino is an unincorporated community in Mendocino County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Mendocino. The name arrived secondhand — borrowed from a cape eighty-five miles up the coast, itself named to flatter a viceroy of New Spain. Out on this headland the Pacific does all the talking, and none of it is to me.

pois.name: Fort Bragg
pois.blurb: Fort Bragg is a city along the North Coast of California in Mendocino County.
pois.beat: Fort Bragg. The sea sits eighty-five feet below the whole city and keeps the receipts — salt on the air thick enough to start rumors about my rocker panels. I won't stay parked long.

pois.name: Eureka, CA
pois.blurb: Eureka is a city in and the county seat of Humboldt County, located on the North Coast of California.
pois.beat: Eureka. This is where California stops pretending to hurry — two hundred seventy miles past San Francisco, a hundred short of Oregon, fog working Humboldt Bay like it's owed something. 101 runs straight through; so could I.

pois.name: Weed
pois.blurb: Weed is a city in Siskiyou County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Weed. Half the map out here answers to this name — Edgewood, Carrick, Lake Shastina, all taking their mail addressed to Weed, like the word has its own gravity. Some names you don't escape. I'd know.

pois.name: Mount Shasta
pois.blurb: Mount Shasta is a city in Siskiyou County, California, United States, at approximately 3,600 feet (1,100 m) above sea level on the flanks of Mount Shasta, a prominent northern Cal…
pois.beat: Mount Shasta, the city — nine miles from the summit of the volcano it answers to, which makes the mountain less a view than a landlord. The air runs thin up here; my carburetors noticed before I did.

pois.name: Yreka
pois.blurb: Yreka is a city in and the county seat of Siskiyou County, California, United States, near the Shasta River and approximately 22 miles south of the state border with Oregon.
pois.beat: Yreka. County seat of Siskiyou, twenty-two miles short of the Oregon line — close enough that the border feels like a mood instead of a law. One more tank of gas in this state; I intend to spend it well.

pois.name: Susanville
pois.blurb: Susanville is the only incorporated city in Lassen County, California, United States, of which it is also the county seat.
pois.beat: Susanville. Lassen County managed to incorporate exactly one city, and this is it — which sounds like an honor until you realize nobody else applied. High-desert dark out here; my headlights feel personal.

pois.name: Alturas
pois.blurb: Alturas is the only incorporated city in Modoc County, California, United States, of which it is also the county seat.
pois.beat: Alturas. Two forks of the Pit River shake hands here, north and south, and in Modoc County that counts as a crowd. Quiet enough to hear my own valvetrain; I don't hate it.

pois.name: Chico
pois.blurb: Chico is the most populous city in Butte County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Chico. A hundred and one thousand people, which after the high desert reads less like a city than a change of climate. First stoplight in hours — I sit through it twice, relearning patience.

pois.name: Placerville
pois.blurb: Placerville is a city in and the county seat of El Dorado County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Placerville. The county styled itself El Dorado and the town keeps placer gold right in its name — ten thousand people still living downstream of a very old bet. Some wagers take a century to settle.

pois.name: Nevada City
pois.blurb: Nevada City is a city in and the county seat of Nevada County, California, United States, 60 miles (97 km) northeast of Sacramento, 84 miles (135 km) southwest of Reno and 147 mil…
pois.beat: Nevada City. A California town wearing Nevada's name, eighty-four miles from the actual Reno as if to maximize the confusion. The pines crowd the road in early, and the dark behind them is older than the town.

pois.name: Sonora
pois.blurb: Sonora is the only incorporated city in Tuolumne County, California, United States, of which it is also the county seat.
pois.beat: Sonora. Founded by Mexican miners who carried the name of home north through a gold rush and set it down here for keeps. You can pan everything out of a river except where you're from.

pois.name: Mariposa
pois.blurb: Mariposa is an unincorporated community and census-designated place (CDP) in and the county seat of Mariposa County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Mariposa. Named for the monarchs that overwinter here — something that small, finding the same town every year without a map. I navigate by satellite and I'm in no position to judge.

pois.name: Oakhurst
pois.blurb: Oakhurst is a census-designated place (CDP) in Madera County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Oakhurst. Highway 41 meets Highway 49 here, and every car in the foothills has to choose a future at that junction. Mine chose itself miles back; I just kept the wheels under it.

pois.name: Modesto
pois.blurb: Modesto is the county seat of and the largest city in Stanislaus County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Modesto. Nineteenth-largest city in California — the demographic middle lane, held at a steady seventy, no signal, no apology. I've always respected anything that knows its lane and stays in it.

pois.name: Visalia
pois.blurb: Visalia is a city in the agricultural San Joaquin Valley of California.
pois.beat: Visalia, deep in the San Joaquin's farm country, where the dust on my windshield isn't dirt — it's inventory, the whole valley airborne one acre at a time. Wipers are a negotiation, not a solution.

pois.name: Zzyzx
pois.blurb: Zzyzx, formerly Soda Springs, is an unincorporated place in San Bernardino County, California, United States, within the boundaries of the Mojave National Preserve, managed by the…
pois.beat: There used to be a mineral springs and health spa out here — which tells you everything about the kind of man who looks at the Mojave and sees a cure. Zzyzx. The springs are gone; the name kept the fever.

pois.name: Amboy
pois.blurb: Amboy is an unincorporated community in San Bernardino County, in California's Mojave Desert, west of Needles and east of Ludlow on historic Route 66.
pois.beat: Amboy. The entire business district is a post office, a motel-diner, and a shop selling Route 66 back to the people driving it. The road ate its towns; this one survived by becoming the menu.

pois.name: Tecopa
pois.blurb: Tecopa is a census-designated place (CDP) in the Mojave Desert in southeast Inyo County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Tecopa, population one hundred twenty. At that size a town isn't a place so much as an agreement, and everyone here has read the terms. I kill the headlights out of courtesy.

pois.name: Koreatown
pois.blurb: Koreatown is a neighborhood in central Los Angeles, California, centered near Sixth and Alexandria streets.
pois.beat: Sixth and Alexandria — the maps call this the center of Koreatown, but a neighborhood like this doesn't have a center, it has a pulse. Steam on the glass, neon in the paint.

pois.name: Venice Beach
pois.blurb: Venice is a neighborhood of the City of Los Angeles within the Westside region of Los Angeles County, California, United States.
pois.beat: Venice. Technically a neighborhood of Los Angeles, which is like calling a stray cat technically somebody's pet. The Westside ends where the pavement starts smelling of salt.

pois.name: Malibu
pois.blurb: Malibu is a beach city in the Santa Monica Mountains region of Los Angeles County, California, United States, about 30 miles (48 km) west of Los Angeles.
pois.beat: Malibu. Twenty-one miles of beaches, every foot owned by somebody who calls the ocean a view. The Pacific doesn't take it personally — it does the same work for everyone.

pois.name: Yuma
pois.blurb: Yuma is a city in and the county seat of Yuma County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Yuma grew by twenty-five hundred people in a decade, says the census — expansion at the speed of someone deciding to stay. I'm only passing through, which keeps the average honest.

pois.name: Quartzsite
pois.blurb: Quartzsite is a town in La Paz County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: The census found 2,413 people in Quartzsite, which out here reads less like a statistic and more like a roll call. Take fuel while it's offered — the desert past town isn't running a charity.

pois.name: Parker
pois.blurb: Parker is a town in and the county seat of La Paz County, Arizona, United States, on the Colorado River in Parker Valley.
pois.beat: Parker. The Colorado River slides past town the way money moves past most people — close enough to touch, gone before you do. I park nose-out where I can hear the water.

pois.name: Bullhead City
pois.blurb: Bullhead City is a city located on the Colorado River in Mohave County, Arizona, United States, 97 miles (156 km) south of Las Vegas, Nevada, and directly across the Colorado Rive…
pois.beat: The casinos are across the river in Laughlin; the paychecks sleep on this side. Bullhead City — Nevada keeps the neon, Arizona keeps the alarm clocks, and the Colorado runs between them declining to comment.

pois.name: Oatman
pois.blurb: Oatman is a census-designated place (CDP) in the Black Mountains of Mohave County, Arizona, United States, at an elevation of 2,710 feet (830 m).
pois.beat: Oatman. Two prospectors struck ten million in gold here in 1915 — the kind of luck that builds a town overnight and bills it for a century. My carburetors don't love the climb. We manage.

pois.name: Seligman
pois.blurb: Seligman is a census-designated place (CDP) on the northern border of Yavapai County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Seligman. One of the stops old Route 66 still owns up to — the interstate took the traffic and left the loyalty. Engines sound different on a road that remembers what they're for.

pois.name: Prescott
pois.blurb: Prescott is a city in and the county seat of Yavapai County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Prescott. Population 45,827, counted to the last soul, like the town wanted credit for each one. After the open road, that kind of precision feels like being watched.

pois.name: Jerome
pois.blurb: Jerome is a town in the Black Hills of Yavapai County in the U.S.
pois.beat: Jerome. The whole town is stapled to the side of Cleopatra Hill, streets switchbacked like somebody's second thoughts. My brakes and I are renegotiating our relationship.

pois.name: Payson
pois.blurb: Payson is a town in northern Gila County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Payson. They call it the Heart of Arizona for sitting near the dead center of the map — cartography flattering itself into poetry. Still, the middle of anywhere is a fine place to be nobody.

pois.name: Show Low
pois.blurb: Show Low is a city in Navajo County, Arizona.
pois.beat: Show Low. The sign claims 6,345 feet and my carburetors corroborate — thin air, lean mixture, no secrets at this altitude. Everything runs a little lean up here, including me.

pois.name: Holbrook
pois.blurb: Holbrook is a city in Navajo County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Holbrook. County seat of Navajo County — the paperwork has to live somewhere, and it chose a town of 4,858. Out here the horizon does most of the governing anyway.

pois.name: Winslow
pois.blurb: Winslow is a city in Navajo County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Winslow. 57 miles from Flagstaff, 240 from Albuquerque, 329 from Las Vegas — a town defined entirely by how far it is from everywhere else. I respect that in a place.

pois.name: Window Rock
pois.blurb: Window Rock, known in Navajo as Tségháhoodzání, is a city and census-designated place that serves as the capital of the Navajo Nation, the largest Native American tribe by both la…
pois.beat: Window Rock. Tségháhoodzání — capital of the Navajo Nation, the largest nation by land and by people both. Most road atlases shade it and move on. The atlases are wrong to.

pois.name: Chinle
pois.blurb: Chinle is a census-designated place (CDP) in Apache County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Chinle. The name is Navajo for 'flowing out' — this is where the water leaves Canyon de Chelly and decides what to be next. I know something about exiting a narrow place at speed.

pois.name: Kayenta
pois.blurb: Kayenta is a U.S.
pois.beat: Kayenta. The only township under Navajo Nation law — a legal category with exactly one member, established 1986 and never duplicated. I have a weakness for things that exist in editions of one.

pois.name: Tuba City
pois.blurb: Tuba City is an unincorporated town and census-designated place in Coconino County, Arizona, on the Navajo Nation, United States.
pois.beat: Tuba City. Second-largest community in Coconino County, which says more about the county than the town. Out here, size is measured in miles between gas pumps. I take the hint and top off.

pois.name: Globe
pois.blurb: Globe is a city in and the county seat of Gila County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Globe. A mining camp from around 1875 that never quite changed out of its work clothes. Towns like this don't perform for visitors, which is its own kind of welcome.

pois.name: Superior
pois.blurb: Superior is a town in northern Pinal County, Arizona, United States, and is the oldest town in the county.
pois.beat: Superior. When the Silver King played out, the town switched to copper at the Magma without breaking stride. I admire anything that retools to survive. It's how you get to be old.

pois.name: Bisbee
pois.blurb: Bisbee is a city in and the county seat of Cochise County in southeastern Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Bisbee. The census says 652 fewer people than the decade before, and the town wears the subtraction quietly. Emptying places have the best acoustics. An engine sounds honest here.

pois.name: Tombstone
pois.blurb: Tombstone is a city in Cochise County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Tombstone. Somewhere between forty and eighty-five million in silver came out of this dirt, and nobody kept books straight enough to say which. Rich strikes never do.

pois.name: Willcox
pois.blurb: Willcox is a city in Cochise County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Willcox. The Sulphur Springs Valley runs flat to every horizon, dotted with lakes that only bother existing part of the year. I understand intermittent things. Half my gauges are the same way.

pois.name: Ajo
pois.blurb: Ajo is an unincorporated community in Pima County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Ajo. State Route 85, forty-three miles from Mexico, and the road south doesn't pretend it's going anywhere else. I idle a little quieter this close to a border.

pois.name: Why
pois.blurb: Why is an unincorporated rural community in Pima County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Why. The town, not the question — though thirty miles from the Mexican border, the distinction wears thin. Top off here; the desert south of this doesn't negotiate.

pois.name: Gila Bend
pois.blurb: Gila Bend, founded in 1872, is a town in Maricopa County, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Gila Bend. The river hits a ninety-degree turn here, like it saw something downstream it wanted no part of, and the town settled in at the elbow. Rivers get to change their minds; roads have to commit.

pois.name: Casa Grande
pois.blurb: Casa Grande is a city in Pinal County, approximately halfway between Phoenix and Tucson, in the U.S.
pois.beat: Casa Grande. Spanish for 'big house,' named for ruins that actually sit in Coolidge, one town over. Imagine building your whole name on something that was never yours. Anyway.

pois.name: Wickenburg
pois.blurb: Wickenburg is a town in Maricopa and Yavapai counties, Arizona, United States.
pois.beat: Wickenburg, straddling Maricopa and Yavapai counties — one town, two sets of paperwork, the line running somewhere under the asphalt. Some places never pick a lane. Professionally, I sympathize.

pois.name: Provo
pois.blurb: Provo is a city in and the county seat of Utah County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Provo. Fourth-largest city in Utah, and the streets still feel swept by hand. A car my age is conspicuous in a town this tidy, so I'm keeping the revs polite and the idle apologetic.

pois.name: Ogden
pois.blurb: Ogden is a city in and the county seat of Weber County, Utah, United States, located approximately 10 miles (16 km) east of the Great Salt Lake and 40 miles (64 km) north of Salt …
pois.beat: Ogden. Ten miles east of the Great Salt Lake, close enough that the wind off the water gets a vote. Cities that grow up next to something that big learn to keep their own counsel.

pois.name: Logan
pois.blurb: Logan is a city in Cache County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Logan. The metro here spills clean over the state line into Franklin County, Idaho — the valley never agreed to the survey. Cold air pools in places like this. So do quiet people.

pois.name: Tooele
pois.blurb: Tooele is a city in Tooele County in the U.S.
pois.beat: Tooele. The town is known for its Army Depot — a careful way of saying the government stores things out here it doesn't want closer to the city. Nobody elaborates. I respect that in a place.

pois.name: Wendover
pois.blurb: Wendover is a city on the western edge of Tooele County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Wendover. Eleven hundred people holding down the spot where Utah runs out of itself. Towns at the end of a state idle like a held breath. I fit right in.

pois.name: Price
pois.blurb: Price is a city in the U.S.
pois.beat: Price. There's a prehistoric museum here, USU Eastern's — a town that keeps its oldest residents on display and doesn't blink. Against that scale, fifty-four years of steel is a rumor. Refreshing.

pois.name: Helper
pois.blurb: Helper is a city in Carbon County, Utah, United States, approximately 110 miles (180 km) southeast of Salt Lake City and 7 miles (11 km) northwest of the city of Price.
pois.beat: Helper. Seven miles northwest of Price, named like a job title nobody holds anymore. I trust a town that admits, right there on the sign, what it was for. Most places dress it up.

pois.name: Green River
pois.blurb: Green River is a city in Emery County, Utah United States.
pois.beat: Green River. Eight hundred forty-seven people, one river, and the long quiet of Emery County between them. The water's just passing through. Tonight, so am I.

pois.name: Hanksville
pois.blurb: Hanksville is a small town in Wayne County, Utah, United States, at the junction of State Routes 24 and 95.
pois.beat: Hanksville. State Routes 24 and 95 meet here and call it a town; out where pavement is this scarce, an intersection is a civic achievement. Fill up — I mean it. The map gets theoretical from here.

pois.name: Torrey
pois.blurb: Torrey is a town located on State Route 24 in Wayne County, Utah, United States, 8 miles (13 km) from Capitol Reef National Park.
pois.beat: Torrey. Eight miles from Capitol Reef and wise enough not to compete with it — the town keeps its voice down and lets the rock do the closing. I drop to second and do the same.

pois.name: Escalante
pois.blurb: Escalante is a city in central Garfield County, Utah, United States, located along Utah Scenic Byway 12 (SR-12) in the south-central part of the state.
pois.beat: Escalante. The state calls Route 12 a Scenic Byway, which is bureaucratic for a road that can make you religious. I take the corners reverent through here. The asphalt has earned it.

pois.name: Panguitch
pois.blurb: Panguitch is a city in and the county seat of Garfield County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Panguitch — 'Big Fish' in Southern Paiute, named for lakes where the rainbow trout stay year-round. A town christened for abundance that actually stuck around. Almost nothing does.

pois.name: Beaver
pois.blurb: Beaver is a city in and the county seat of Beaver County in southwestern Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Beaver. The census says 3,592 now, up nearly five hundred from the count before — which out here passes for a boom, and I've never trusted a boom. Growing towns ask questions; shrinking ones wave you through.

pois.name: Fillmore
pois.blurb: Fillmore is a city in and the county seat of Millard County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Fillmore. They split the thirteenth president in two out here — the county took Millard, the town took Fillmore — and neither half gets remembered much. There are worse afterlives than becoming geography.

pois.name: Delta
pois.blurb: Delta is the largest city in Millard County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Delta. Farmland in every direction — green squares pressed out of the desert by pure stubbornness, a town that grows things in country that mostly grows distance.

pois.name: Monticello
pois.blurb: Monticello is a city in and the county seat of San Juan County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Monticello. Pioneers set this place down in July 1887 — an honest month to start a town, when the country shows you exactly what you're agreeing to. They stayed anyway; I'm only passing through.

pois.name: Blanding
pois.blurb: Blanding is a city in San Juan County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Blanding. Settled by Mormon families from the famed Hole-In-The-Rock expedition — a name that admits the way in was the hard part. I keep to the pavement, feeling a little soft about it.

pois.name: Bluff
pois.blurb: Bluff is a town in San Juan County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Bluff. Incorporated 2018 — meaning this town held off on being official for about as long as the law allows. Anywhere that suspicious of paperwork has my sympathy.

pois.name: Mexican Hat
pois.blurb: Mexican Hat is a census-designated place (CDP) in Utah in the United States.
pois.beat: Mexican Hat. Twenty-one residents at the last census — a number small enough that everyone here knows the sound of every engine in town, and mine isn't one of them.

pois.name: Hurricane
pois.blurb: Hurricane is a city in Washington County, Utah, United States.
pois.beat: Hurricane. Peach and pecan orchards in a town named for wind — either defiance or a very long joke, and judging by the trees, the joke is holding. Sweet air does strange things to an intake.

pois.name: Vernal
pois.blurb: Vernal is the county seat of and the largest city in Uintah County, Utah, approximately 175 miles (280 km) east of Salt Lake City and 20 miles (32 km) west of the Colorado border.
pois.beat: Vernal. The Colorado line waits twenty miles east, and border towns always feel like waiting rooms — everybody half-arrived or half-gone. We take on fuel and act like we belong.

pois.name: Heber City
pois.blurb: Heber City is a city and county seat of Wasatch County, Utah.
pois.beat: Heber City. Forty-three miles southeast of Salt Lake — close enough to feel the city breathing, far enough to deny it. Forty-three miles isn't geography; it's a decision.

pois.name: Hayward
pois.blurb: An East Bay flatland city of warehouses and bay mud — and, in a low building off the freeway, the Zoox robotaxi works.

pois.name: Santa Nella
pois.blurb: An I-5 pit stop in the Central Valley flats, famous for one thing: Pea Soup Andersen's, green soup and a windmill since 1924.

pois.name: Black Rock City (off-season)
pois.blurb: The Black Rock playa, 50 weeks a year just cracked white nothing to the curve of the earth — no city, no people, only the ghost of one and a wind that carries strange things.
